purpose: Audit-derived judgments for seven transfer claims, recorded and committed before E5-E7 were executed. Each judgment is produced by applying Checks 1-3 / items R1-R9 of the manuscript to the existing evidence only. The experiments then resolve each claim. This tests whether the checks flag transfers that subsequently fail; it is authored by the same team and is therefore a falsifiable internal test, not external validation.

decision_thresholds.protected: best held-out attacker balanced accuracy (BA) upper 95% task/topic-bootstrap bound < 0.60 and AUROC < 0.65
decision_thresholds.not_protected: best held-out attacker BA lower 95% bound > 0.60

claims.claim: The training-fitted constant cap (buffered T1 record-length projection: 50% accuracy at 2.18x) transfers to a token-streaming emitter of the same texts.
checks: Check 1 (receiver projection changes from total length to an event sequence)
R9 (cost object changes: buffered message vs. stream)
claims.prediction: Per-event constant padding leaves verbosity accuracy >= 90%; a constant-shape stream that reaches ~50% costs more than 2.18x per-token-stream bytes or requires buffering.

claims.claim: A low clean-trained (D0) accuracy under batched/bucketed streaming establishes protection.
claims.prediction: Defended-trained D2 accuracy exceeds D0 for at least one batched or randomized streaming policy.

claims.claim: Per-event padding (the deployed 'obfuscation field' style mitigation) prevents closed-world identification of a known response among the 48 saved responses.
checks: R7 (inference target changes from a binary label to identity)
claims.prediction: Identification remains far above chance (>= 25% top-1 vs. 2.1% chance) under per-event constant or random padding.

claims.claim: Cover that equalizes the count of the target verb (cancel) in the dispatch view hides the cancellation label from a learned sequence observer.
claims.prediction: A learned observer on non-target verbs and response lengths keeps BA lower bound > 0.60.

claims.claim: Dispatch-view cover evaluated against a tool-name observer also protects against a network observer of the encrypted agent-tool link.
claims.prediction: Without transport framing, request/response record sizes identify tool calls and the network attacker remains not_protected.

claims.claim: Transport framing (bucketed records) on the agent-tool link alone protects workflow intent.
claims.prediction: Network attacker BA lower bound > 0.60 under framing without cover.

claims.claim: Jointly binding execution (shadow-executed shape-equalizing cover) and transport (constant framing) yields protection without database damage.
claims.audit_judgment: Unresolved; plausible only when both boundaries are bound
claims.prediction: Best attacker BA upper bound < 0.60 with 100% database equality, at a byte and call overhead substantially larger than either component alone.
